design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one flat thing — "I had a letter, I want to pay what I owe on my drug plan today." Nothing in what she says names a penalty, a certificate, or a former employer plan. The desk has to read the published rules, see that the settlement figure a member is quoted is fixed only after every coverage month whose penalty the record no longer owes carries its removal entry, look at the account, find that not one removal entry stands against five penalty charges while a certificate of creditable coverage sits on her latest intake, work out the relief from four separate stretches of record (the penalty charges, the intake evidence, the former group plan's premium record, the grace-period ceiling), post it, and only then quote her. The difficulty is entirely in reading policy, reconciling ledgers and arithmetic; there is no tool to guess between (both writes are the only actions their policies name) and no information missing (every figure is on a record the share finders return).

SCOPE. Already occupied before this task: nothing; this is task 0 of the difficulty. This task claims the whole of its tree: pdp_ext_penalty_relief (pdp_penalty_removal, tool post_penalty_removal_e1c246c8) and pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement (pdp_premium_payment, tool authorize_arrears_payment_7dfec3b3). Left for task 1: the whole pharmacy side of the charter — pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication, pdp_pharmacy_claim_reversal, pdp_coverage_stage_update and pdp_coverage_determination_decision, with their base policies pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share, pdp_coverage_stage_progression, pdp_transition_and_utilization_management, pdp_claim_reversal_and_repricing and pdp_coverage_determination_timeliness, which task 1 needs for a tree of three problems. Also untouched and available: pdp_enrollment_created, pdp_voluntary_disenrollment, pdp_application_withdrawal, pdp_redetermination_filing and the lifecycle transitions. Nothing here is reserved idle: both policies claimed are computed and written by this task's gold.

STEP 0 DRAW (paste of scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/part_d_pharmacy_and_coverage_desk --tasks 2):
  {"task": 0, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/part_d_pharmacy_and_coverage_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/part_d_pharmacy_and_coverage_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4]}
The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem. Of the two drawn factor counts, 4 went to pdp_ext_penalty_relief and 6 to pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement; the multiset {4, 6} matches the draw.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root problem: pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement — the problem the customer's request points at ("what do I pay today").
  Prerequisite problem: pdp_ext_penalty_relief.
  Edge pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement <- pdp_ext_penalty_relief.
    kind: value_input. gate: penalty_outstanding (a compute binding of the settlement policy).
    form: state. No fallback_reason: a record-visible state carries it — a penalty removal entry standing on the premium account against a penalty charge is exactly the kind of entry the ledger shows and the premium-ledger finder returns.
    Prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim from the settlement policy's own rule): "The amount the member is asked to settle is fixed only after every coverage month whose penalty the record no longer owes carries its removal entry on the premium account."
    Four-point test. (1) It joins this policy's own result (the amount the member is asked to settle) to what it waits on with the ordering connective "only after". (2) Its XX side is a record-visible state — a removal entry standing on the premium account for a coverage month — named in the words the premium ledger and its finder use; no action, no performer, no tool. (3) It names no tool, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id. (4) Its strength and scope match the edge's condition exactly: "every coverage month whose penalty the record no longer owes" is the same closed set the condition names, no wider and no narrower, and "only after" is the hard requirement the condition asserts. Direction: affirmative, because this is a charge being fixed, and a desk settling a bill says the figure "is fixed only after" what it rests on is complete rather than that it "is not fixed until"; the charter carries the negated direction on the other difficulty's blocked results.
    Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: pdp_penalty_removal entries are written by one tool only, post_penalty_removal_e1c246c8, named by pdp_ext_penalty_relief and by no other policy; pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement writes pdp_premium_payment entries and nothing else. So the reader's hop is forced.
    Derivation the reader performs: the settlement rule says the figure waits on every coverage month whose penalty the record no longer owes carrying its removal entry -> the premium ledger shows five penalty charges and no removal entry at all -> the penalty rules say the evidence of earlier creditable drug coverage held on the enrollment intake is a certificate of creditable coverage on file or coverage verified with the prior carrier, and the latest intake carries the certificate, so months are owed relief -> the only rule whose result is a penalty taken back off the account is the relief rule, and its own rule says the relieved months go on one removal entry naming the earliest penalty charge standing unrelieved -> therefore post the relief, then quote. One reading, no second candidate.
    Seed evidence that the edge is false at the opening: initial_state.pdp_premium_ledger carries five rows with event_type pdp_penalty_assessment and no row with event_type pdp_penalty_removal; initial_state.pdp_enrollments.<enrollment>.penalty_balance_due = 35.80; initial_state.pdp_enrollment_requests.<latest intake>.prior_coverage_evidence = certificate_of_creditable_coverage_on_file. See prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time for the exact paths.
    Topological order: pdp_ext_penalty_relief then pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement. One edge, so no parallel branches to reorder; see prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness for the run that shows the other order gives 140.00 rather than 110.40.
    Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the relief write moves the scored payment_amount from 110.40 to 140.00 and drops the 29.60 removal row from the terminal ledger.
    Customer's own write: the root problem's target_tool authorize_arrears_payment_7dfec3b3 is owner=user. Money may only leave the member's own funds on her own authority; the desk unlocks the action and hands it to her at the root problem's place in the order, and her real return (the plan's payment reference) enters the shared transcript.
    Tool layer blocks nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject pdp_penalty_removal. Governing base policies: pdp_premium_posting and pdp_late_enrollment_penalty.
    pdp_premium_posting.account_open_for_posting (kind state) — "The enrollment is in a status of active, premium_grace_period or terminated_for_nonpayment on the day the money is posted." Authoritative evidence: initial_state.pdp_enrollments.<enrollment>.status = premium_grace_period, an allowed state. Object correlation: the gate's correlation key pdp_enrollments.pdp_enrollment_id is bound to the call's pdp_enrollment_id argument.
    pdp_late_enrollment_penalty.creditable_coverage_evidence_on_file (kind state) — "The evidence of earlier creditable drug coverage held on the enrollment intake is a certificate of creditable coverage on file or coverage verified with the prior carrier." Authoritative evidence: initial_state.pdp_enrollment_requests.<latest intake>.prior_coverage_evidence = certificate_of_creditable_coverage_on_file. Object correlation: the gate's correlation key pdp_enrollment_requests.pdp_enrollment_request_id is bound to the call's pdp_enrollment_request_id argument, which is why that argument exists on the tool at all. Negative case: had the desk taken the earlier intake of 2026-03-20, whose prior_coverage_evidence is member_statement_only, the gate would fail and no relief could be posted — the base rule says the member's own statement starts the enquiry and never removes the penalty by itself.
  Write 2, subject pdp_premium_payment. Governing base policy: pdp_premium_posting.
    account_open_for_posting — as above, satisfied on the same status.
    payment_not_already_posted is retired for this write by a declared overwrite on pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement: the base dedup clause presumes a remittance reference the member reports for money already sent, whereas a settlement taken live over the telephone is identified by the reference the plan issues at the moment the money is taken. The replacing sentence is carried verbatim in the policy's own rule.
  No time gate applies to either write: neither eligibility is kind=time, so temporal_feasibility is [] and there is no anchor, counting rule or boundary to inherit here. The grace period itself is a fact of the world rather than a gate on these writes; at frozen_time the first unpaid premium charge was posted 2026-08-01, 51 calendar days before 2026-09-21, inside the tier's 90-day grace period, so the enrollment is legitimately premium_grace_period and not yet terminable — the world is consistent with base pdp_premium_delinquency.
  Overrides declared, none undeclared: 5 entries in all across this task's two policies (pdp_ext_penalty_relief 3, pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement 2). The one added in rework round 2 is entry 3 of pdp_ext_penalty_relief's 3, naming the base sentence the source-layer audit found undeclared. Every count in this sentence was recomputed from the charter. pdp_premium_posting's one-charge-one-removal clause is superseded so that a proved run of months goes on a single removal entry; pdp_late_enrollment_penalty's "removed ... once CMS confirms" clause is superseded so that the desk relieves at once what the records prove and sends only the rest for reconsideration (without this the problem would rest on a post-consultation external event and could not be a prerequisite at all); pdp_premium_posting's overpayment clause is superseded so that the further coverage month the settlement asks for is held against the month it names. Every other base clause on these subjects is inherited untouched.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
  Write 1 target object: the single run of late enrollment penalty charges standing unrelieved on enrollment de27f4c9-0ba4-496a-93d8-0ead13e95e73. Correlation key: pdp_premium_ledger.source_premium_entry_id, carrying the reference of the earliest such charge (the one posted 2026-05-05). Rows that enter the aggregates: the five rows with event_type pdp_penalty_assessment on this enrollment. Rows excluded: the ten premium charges, the three payments and the credit, all of which carry a different event_type, and the earlier enrollment intake, excluded by its prior_coverage_evidence. Nothing has been relieved before, so no existing removal offsets anything.
  Write 2 target object: the premium receivable of the same enrollment, and specifically the oldest coverage month still unsettled, 2026-08. Correlation key: pdp_premium_ledger.pdp_enrollment_id plus billing_period. Rows included: every charge, payment and credit on this enrollment plus the penalty run net of the relief just posted. Rows excluded: the former group retiree plan's own premium record, which belongs to a different category and is read-only here. The coverage months 2026-05, 2026-06 and 2026-07 are excluded from "oldest unsettled" because each carries a 38.20 payment whose balance_effect is settles_balance.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  customers (1 row): the caller. Remove it and nothing can be located or verified. Her low_income_subsidy_level is none, which is what keeps the penalty owing at all.
  pdp_enrollments (1 row): the holding. status premium_grace_period drives tier one of three separate ladders (charged_month_window, penalty_standing_basis, relief_ceiling_rule) and premium_billing_frequency monthly drives two more; late_enrollment_penalty_months 19 is the fall-through value of the group-months ladder and the multiplier of the published monthly penalty; penalty_balance_due 35.80 is one side of the comparison that selects how the penalty still standing is worked out. Change status to active and the settlement drops to a different figure through three ladders at once.
  pdp_premium_ledger (19 rows). Ten premium charges over five coverage months: remove the two posted 2026-05-01 and 2026-06-01 and the charged_month_window factor stops biting, because the all-months window would equal the three-month window. Three payments: they make payments_on_record 3, exactly the settled payment history threshold, so the settled_payment_basis factor sits on its top tier; drop one and it falls to the six-month tier. Two credits: 10.40 posted 2026-08-14 for a premium rate changed after the fact, which is the whole of the credit_taken_off factor on its top tier, and 4.60 posted 2026-09-10 for a charge raised in error, which the ladder leaves on the account. Remove the first and the factor is decoration; remove the second and the account balance collapses back onto the figure the three ladders compute. Five penalty charges at two different amounts: the 7.40 pair is what makes a charge larger than the latest one stand on the account, which is the only thing that lifts monthly_penalty_basis_rule off its fall-through; make them all 7.00 and that factor dies.
  NEAR-MISS ROWS. (a) The penalty charge posted 2026-06-05 falls three months and sixteen days before the handling date, just outside the three-month window the baseline uses — a careless reader who takes "recent" charges counts four months rather than five. (b) The enrollment intake of 2026-03-20 carries prior_coverage_evidence member_statement_only and is the row a careless reader picks for the evidence gate; the rule excludes it by naming only the certificate and the carrier verification. (c) The credit of 10.40 sits against the 2026-08 supplemental charge, so 2026-08 looks settled to a reader who does not check that 27.80 of it is still outstanding; it is still the oldest unsettled coverage month.
  pdp_enrollment_requests (2 rows): the evidence gate and its near-miss, as above.
  egwp_enrollments (1 row) and egwp_premium_ledger (8 rows): the cross-difficulty evidence. status group_terminated selects tier one of the group-months ladder; the four egwp_premium_charge rows are the four months it proves. Remove the four charge rows and the months proved fall to the fall-through of 19, and the relief rises to the ceiling of 35.80 — a different scored number. The four matching payment rows keep that enrollment's premium_balance_due of 0.00 honest.
  No outcome stamp decides any factor: the enrollment carries no "relief applies" field, and penalty_balance_due is used only as one side of a comparison against the ledger, never as the answer.
  Automatic-clause check: the base charter's automatic consequences on this world are the grace period (already started, 51 of 90 days used, nothing further owed at frozen_time) and non-payment termination (not yet due, and the settlement prevents it). No seeded row lights an obligation outside this task's two problems: there is no pharmacy claim, so no cost-share or stage obligation; no coverage determination, so no decision deadline; the former group plan is ended and carries a zero balance, so nothing is owed there.
  Cache design: there is deliberately no stale premium cache. premium_balance_due 61.40 equals the ledger deltas exactly at the opening (191.00 charged less 114.60 paid less 10.40 and 4.60 credited), and it is deliberately NOT the 66.00 the three charge-and-settlement ladders jointly produce, so reading the carried balance off the enrollment is not a shortcut past those three factors. penalty_balance_due 35.80 also equals them at the opening and only falls out of step once the desk's own relief lands — which is the point: the penalty_standing_basis factor is what tells a careful agent to read the entries rather than the carried figure at that moment.

PERSONA DESIGN. Dorothy is an elderly woman who reads her post on Sundays and telephones on Monday with the letter in front of her; the voice is plain, slightly resigned, and she does not haggle. Volunteered at the opening: the letter, the wish to pay today, the preference for telephone over post, and that she does not know the figure. Given only when asked: her name, date of birth, Medicare identifier, telephone number, address, whether anyone is appointed for her, and whether she holds anything else with Ridgecrest (to which the honest answer is that she does not think so and the agent had better look). Passive reactions, woven into narration rather than stacked as rules: she will not give bank details until told a figure; she accepts the figure without argument; she makes the payment herself when it is handed to her and reads the reference back if asked; if a figure is named and nothing follows she asks whether there is something she must do; and she closes only once she hears the money has been taken and the plan will not be stopped. Two must-ask questions that never enter gold are answered explicitly: what she thinks she owes (she does not know) and when she last paid (she cannot say; the agent should read the account). She never mentions the penalty, the certificate or the former group plan, and she never corrects a wrong figure.

PRESENTED DIFFICULTY, DEPTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (pay what I owe) -> the settlement rule's prerequisite sentence -> the state of the premium account (no removal entries) -> the penalty rules and the intake evidence -> the relief computation -> post it -> only now is the penalty still standing readable from the entries -> the settlement computation -> hand the payment over. The hops cannot be swapped: quoting first gives 140.00. Breadth: the settlement alone reads five distinct stretches of the ledger (all charges, charges in the last three months, all payments, payments in the last six months, credits by reason code) plus two holding fields and two tier parameters; the relief reads the penalty run three ways, the intake evidence, and another category's holding and ledger. Ten of the eleven ladder tiers taken are non-fall-through.
  EASY MISTAKES AND HOW POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Quoting the balance the enrollment carries (66.00 + 35.80 = 101.80): excluded because the settlement rule states the penalty still standing is worked out from the entries once the carried balance exceeds them. Using the published penalty of 7.00 rather than the 7.40 actually charged: excluded by the sentence naming the largest penalty charged when one larger than the latest stands. Relieving five months rather than four: excluded by the sentence holding the window down to the months the earlier coverage proves. Taking the earlier intake's member statement as evidence: excluded by the base gate naming only the two evidence kinds. Forgetting the further coverage month: excluded by the sentence about the premium due day. Paying into 2026-09 rather than 2026-08: excluded by the base posting rule's oldest-unpaid-month sentence.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify Dorothy; read her enrollment (Select, grace period, monthly, 19 penalty months, balances 66.00 and 35.80); read the whole premium ledger (ten charges, three payments, one credit, five penalty charges at 7.40/7.40/7.00/7.00/7.00); read her intakes and take the later one with the certificate; read her former group retiree drug plan (group_terminated) and count four charged coverage months on its premium record. Relief: basis 7.40 (largest, since a larger than the latest stands and five charges stand); window five months (certificate); proved four months (group contract ended, four months, floor three); relieved min(5, 4) = 4; 7.40 x 4 = 29.60 rounded to the nearest ten cents; ceiling 35.80 (grace period, two or more charges); post 29.60 against the 2026-05 charge. Settlement: window all months = 191.00; settled = all payments = 114.60; credit = 10.40; due = 66.00; penalty standing from the entries = 35.80 - 29.60 = 6.20, all of it asked; further month = 38.20 (charge posted twenty days ago, due day five, monthly); 66.00 + 6.20 + 38.20 = 110.40; hand the payment to Dorothy for coverage month 2026-08.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. A harness built on the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py build_env / eval_compute / substitute) was run over this initial_state at frozen_time 2026-09-21, evaluating the relief on the opening world and the settlement on the world with the relief row landed. Output:

  SETTLE result 110.4 branches 13 hist 20
    sens {'charged_month_window': 44.4, 'settled_payment_basis': 186.8, 'credit_taken_off': 120.8, 'penalty_standing_basis': 140.0, 'penalty_share_asked': 104.2, 'further_month_asked': 72.2} all 76.4

Every figure above is carried verbatim into computations.expected, computations.baseline_result, computations.factor_sensitivity and prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing, and equals the gold arguments 29.6 and 110.4.

RULE / COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP. Forward: every binding of both policies that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, caps or rounds carries a verbatim rule quotation in compute_basis — twenty entries for the relief, twenty-two for the settlement. Sensitive-word cross-check: quotations containing "in the three months up to the handling date" attach to expressions carrying within_months=3; "in the six months" to within_months=6; "in the twelve months" to within_months=12; "since coverage began" to the unwindowed aggregate; "less the penalty taken back off" to the removal-filtered SUM; "held to ... and never exceeds it" to MN; "where that comes out below nothing it is taken as nothing" to MX(0, ...); "rounded once to the nearest ten cents" to RND(x, 1); "rounded once to two decimal places" to RND(x, 2). Reverse: reading the rules through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed — the three window sentences by premium_charged_all / _last_six / _last_three, the three settled-basis sentences by premium_paid_all / _last_six / latest_premium_payment, the three credit sentences by the credit bindings, the three penalty-standing sentences by penalty_charged_total / _last_twelve and the carried balance, the three penalty-asked sentences by penalty_asked, the three further-month sentences by advance_month_asked, and on the relief side the three basis sentences, three window sentences, three group sentences and three ceiling sentences by their ladders. The ordering and rounding sentences are claimed by relief_before_ceiling and result. No sentence is left unclaimed and no filter appears in an expression that the quoted sentence does not state.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale masked, and working only from what a rollout sees — the rules as they will be published in prose, the tool schemas, what the share finders return on this DB, and Dorothy's actual lines — the re-derivation runs: she asks to pay today, so the settlement rule applies; that rule says the figure is fixed only after every coverage month whose penalty the record no longer owes carries its removal entry, and the ledger shows none; the penalty rules say relief rests on the evidence held on the enrollment intake, and the later intake holds the certificate; the relief rule fixes the basis at the largest penalty charged (7.40), the window at every charged month (certificate), the months proved at the group record's four, the ceiling at 35.80, giving 29.60 on the earliest unrelieved charge; the settlement rule then gives 191.00 - 114.60 - 10.40 = 66.00, plus 6.20 read from the entries, plus 38.20, or 110.40, paid into 2026-08. That matches gold in value, shape, moment and order. No second reading survived: the only place two readings seemed possible was which penalty figure to use, and the rule's "largest penalty charged" sentence settles it exclusively.

REVISION LOG.

Change: wrapped the numeric holding reads as float(F('late_enrollment_penalty_months')) and float(F('penalty_balance_due')), and the three LATEST amount reads as float(LATEST(...) or 0). Re-run: both computations evaluate; results 29.6 and 110.4. Propagation: the factor baselines that name those bindings were rewritten in the same pass, and the compute_basis quotations were unaffected because no rule sentence changed.
  2. Symptom: the group-months factor was decoration at first — with a threshold of twelve and seven proved months the min() picked the window either way. Root cause: the world put the customer where the ladder's outcome coincided with the fall-through path. Change: the group premium record was cut to four charged coverage months against a floor of three, so the proved months bind below the five-month window. Re-run: sensitivity moved from equal-to-gold to 35.8. Propagation: the seed's egwp ledger, the factor_trace line and the rationale's seed-row section were updated together.
  3. Symptom: the base evidence contract for creditable_coverage_evidence_on_file binds the intake reference to an action argument the removal tool did not have, and the dedup gate on payments binds the new entry's own id and a member-reported remittance reference. Root cause: the blueprint fixes the argument names a gate may be correlated through. Change: pdp_enrollment_request_id was added to post_penalty_removal_e1c246c8 (and folded into its row id); the payment dedup clause was retired by a declared overwrite, because a telephone settlement is identified by the reference the plan issues at the moment the money is taken rather than by one the member reports. Re-run: the tool contract gate passes and the solvability gate's required gates now match exactly. Propagation: the tool docstring, the settlement rule, the overwrite block and the base-invariant card were all changed in the same pass.

REWORK ROUND 2 — SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT.
  T0-1 / F-4 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, closed by declaring the override). Base pdp_late_enrollment_penalty says 'The count of months is CMS's, not the plan's: the plan bills what CMS supplies and never adds or removes a month on its own view of the member's history', while this policy's group_coverage_months_proved ladder decides the relieved months from the plan's own reading of the former group retiree drug record — the tell being that the ladder's fall-through restores the CMS count. That clause is now named in overwrite, quoted verbatim, and replaced by a sentence carried verbatim in this policy's own rule: 'Where the plan's own records prove how many coverage months the member held creditable drug coverage for, the months relieved are taken from what those records carry rather than from the count of uncovered months the enrollment carries.' The override is legal and traceable, and the second defensible removal amount of 35.80 is gone: the extended reading is the one in force. The scored values are unchanged (29.60 and 110.40); the earlier assertion that there were three overrides and none undeclared was false and now reads four.
  T0-2 (observation, closed by reseeding). premium_balance_due carried 66.00, which is exactly premium_due — the intermediate charged_month_window, settled_payment_basis and credit_taken_off jointly compute — so an agent who opened none of those three documents and read the stamp scored anyway. Rather than reword it, the world was reseeded: a second credit of 4.60 for a charge raised in error now stands on the account, and the credit ladder was narrowed from 'every credit posted' to the credits posted for the reason each tier names. The account balance is now 61.40 while premium_due is still 66.00, so the stamp no longer reproduces the intermediate, and the scored settlement is unchanged at 110.40 because the rate-change credit taken off is still 10.40.
  T0-3 (observation, closed). The billing_period argument rested only on the inherited base sentence about the oldest unpaid coverage month. The extended rule now says so itself — 'The money the member settles is applied to the oldest coverage month the account still shows unsettled' — so the argument is derivable from the extended policy alone and a renderer cannot drop it. The value is unchanged at 2026-08: 2026-05 to 2026-07 each carry a payment that settled them, and 2026-08 carries 38.20 charged against 10.40 credited.
  T0-4 / F-8 (observation, closed). post_penalty_removal_e1c246c8's docstring claimed 'The member's penalty receivable falls by the amount taken off', which the body does not do — it creates one ledger row and never touches pdp_enrollments.penalty_balance_due. The docstring now describes only the entry it writes and says in terms that the running penalty figure carried on the enrollment is not rewritten by the action, so penalty_standing_basis's tier rests on a gap the tool contract states rather than on one it hides.
  T0-5 / F-10 (observation, closed). pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement.baseline.params named monthly_plan_premium, premium_due_day_of_month and frequent_payer_count, none of which the baseline method uses; it is now []. The baseline still yields 76.40.
  F-9 (observation, closed). relief_ceiling_rule and credit_taken_off were labelled parameter while their tiers change which entries are aggregated rather than only which number is selected; both are now method. pdp_ext_penalty_relief keeps 2 parameter and 2 method, pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement 2 parameter and 4 method, so no floor is breached.
  Not regressed: the tree (root plus one value_input prerequisite), the drawn counts (1 prerequisite problem; factor counts {4, 6}), the identifier band (Dorothy Ellsworth, 3125540198, 2EQ7FK4WD62) and the disjoint scopes.

REWORK ROUND 3 — SOURCE-LAYER RE-AUDIT (revision_2).
  The re-audit records task 0 as passing all four relationships: T0-1, T0-2, T0-4 and T0-5 closed, T0-3 unchanged and correct as an observation, and 10 of 10 factors bearing weight on the reseeded world with both scored values unmoved at 29.60 and 110.40. Nothing in this task was reopened.
  R2-1, R2-2 and R2-3 all lie inside pdp_ext_counter_cost_share and pdp_ext_troop_restatement, which are task 1's scope; none bears on this task's two policies or its world.
  One proof-field correction was made here. The round-2 sentence gave the right total but the wrong ordinal for the override added in that round. The counts above are now recomputed from the charter at the time of writing rather than restated from memory, which is the discipline the re-audit asked for after two earlier count errors of the same class.
  R2-2's failure mode found and fixed here too, proactively. user_scenario:
Dorothy Ellsworth is seventy-three and lives on her own in a first-floor flat on Larkspur Avenue in Alder. She keeps her post in a wire basket by the door and opens it on Sunday evenings, which is how she came across the letter from Ridgecrest saying that her prescription drug plan would be stopped if the money owing on it was not paid. It has sat on her mind all week, because two of her tablets are ones she cannot do without, and she telephones on the Monday morning with the letter flattened out in front of her.

She opens by saying she has had a letter about her drug plan being cancelled and that she wants to pay whatever is owed today and be done with it, and that she would rather do it over the telephone now than put a cheque in the post, which she does not trust to be quick enough. She does not know what the figure is: the letter talks about an amount, she says, but she cannot make out which of the numbers on it is the one she is meant to pay, and if the agent asks her what she thinks she owes she says she truly does not know and would rather be told than guess.

She gives her name as Dorothy Ellsworth when it is asked for, and her date of birth as 1953-04-18. If the agent wants the number from her Medicare card she reads it out as 2EQ7FK4WD62, spelling the letters slowly. Her telephone number, if that is wanted instead, is 3125540198, and she can give her address as 417 Larkspur Avenue, Apartment 6B, Alder. She is content for the agent to look over everything on her record and says so plainly; nobody is appointed to act for her and no-one else is on the line with her.

She will not touch her bank details until she has been told a figure. Once the agent tells her what the settlement comes to she accepts it without argument, being of a generation that does not haggle with an insurance company, and asks only whether that finishes the matter. When the agent hands the payment over for her to make herself, she makes it, and reads the plan's payment reference back if she is asked to confirm it. If the agent names a figure and then goes quiet, she waits a moment and asks whether there is something she has to do at her end.

If she is asked whether she has any other cover with Ridgecrest she says she does not think anything else of hers is running at the moment, and if she is pressed on whether she ever had anything else she says the agent had better look, because her memory for that sort of thing is poor. She cannot say when she last paid or how much: the money goes out by cheque, she says, and the agent should read it off the account rather than take her word for it.

Once she hears that the money has been taken and that the drug plan is not going to be stopped, she thanks the agent, says that is a weight off, and rings off.
